clue.text: European Union supporter seizing opening at last

indicators.note: seizing means the first pair of pieces grabs the next one and holds it within

an ally is someone who backs you up

explanation.surface: A pro-Brussels campaigner finally grabs a chance to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Union' tempts as the definition's subject; it is a single abbreviation, and 'seizing' places the opening word right after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean in the end, after some delay; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Queen perform accordingly

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen
to go is to function or work, as in 'the engine won't go'

explanation.surface: A monarch acting according to protocol.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin connective means therefore, hence, consequently; a synonym.

clue.text: Save from rising waves? I'm on ocean

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
from tells us to take the letters out of the following words, where they sit across word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone at sea asks how to save themselves from waves swelling around them.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'from' as a link; it is the extraction signal, taking letters out of the phrase. In a down clue 'rising' then reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut back on spending is to save money; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Conviction that if overturned doesn't change

definitions.note: a firmly held principle or belief is a conviction, and that same word reads identically in reverse

indicators.note: a word unaltered when turned upside down in a down entry reads the same in both directions

parts.note: a firmly held principle or belief is a conviction, and that same word reads identically in reverse

explanation.surface: A firmly held belief that survives any challenge unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, so reversing it in the down light leaves it as it was.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or doctrine one is convinced of; a synonym for firm belief.

clue.text: Bearing left one takes off here?

port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A traveller's manner as they set off somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT is the nautical word for left. The question mark flags a definition by example: a plane takes off from here.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft depart from this place, so it is where one takes off; a playful description.

clue.text: Member's accepting consequence for fictions

indicators.note: accepting means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a leg is a limb or member; the 's gives the S
an end is a result or outcome

explanation.surface: A club member accepting the fallout for telling tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Myths and invented tales are fictions; synonym in the plural.

clue.text: Get oxen advancing, driving initially

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Instructions to a drover on getting the oxen to move.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: a pointed stick to drive oxen forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A prod or spiked stick used to urge cattle onward, which is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: Egg-shaped egg, empty

parts.note: an egg is round like the letter O
void means empty or vacant

explanation.surface: Describes an oval, hollow egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Oval in outline like an egg; the dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Crush pepper finally in food consumed

parts.note: a dish is a prepared item of food

indicators.note: in places the pepper's last letter within the word for consumed

parts.note: eaten means consumed

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of pepper

explanation.surface: Grind pepper into a meal that has been eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush someone's spirit is to dispirit or dismay them; a synonym.

clue.text: Swollen, we hear, producing bellyache

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like the one the clue gives

parts.note: grown means increased or swollen

explanation.definitionFit: To bellyache is informal for grumble or complain; a synonym.

clue.text: Huge riots turned out to be justified

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are overturned and rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Morally right or warranted, as in righteous anger; a synonym.

clue.text: Labour dawdle assuming a victory

parts.note: to trail is to lag behind or dawdle

explanation.surface: The Labour party slowly heading for a win.

clue.text: Archaic old university undecided about wife

indicators.note: about means the undecided word goes round the wife letter

parts.note: torn means unable to decide between options

explanation.surface: An ancient college dithering over a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete, out of date through long use; a synonym for antiquated.

clue.text: Confuse with candid clues occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Frank hints that sometimes muddle the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle or befuddle someone's mind; a synonym.

clue.text: Seeming ordinary, sober around time

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: around means the sober word is wrapped round the time letter

parts.note: sensible means level-headed or sober

explanation.surface: A man appears ordinary and sober all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent rather than real, as in an ostensible reason; a synonym.

clue.text: Dissent could become most derogatory

indicators.note: could become says the letters can be turned into another word

explanation.surface: Disagreement might escalate into the nastiest of remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of a word meaning sneering or disparaging; synonym in the same superlative form.

clue.text: Ecstatic former partner stopped missing husband

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: missing means the husband letter is dropped from the stopped word

parts.note: halted means stopped

explanation.surface: A former spouse calls it off, leaving the husband out of the picture.

clue.text: Place grand in small bet for brag

in says the grand letter goes inside the bet word

parts.note: a wager is a bet
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.definitionFit: Boastful talk or a show-off manner; a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Good chap's sound for Prime Minister

parts.note: a lad is a chap; the 's gives the S
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: A decent man's voice suits the top job.
explanation.walkthrough: William Gladstone was a 19th-century British Prime Minister, four times in office.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian Liberal leader who held the top office; definition by example.

clue.text: Dodgy dealer purchases minute gemstone

indicators.note: purchases means the jumbled dealer takes in the minute letter
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A shady trader buys a tiny jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' gives ERALDE from dealer, and M goes in after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: A green precious stone, one example of a gem.

clue.text: Alight from French TGV?

parts.note: de is the French word for from
the TGV is France's high-speed train

explanation.surface: Asks how to get off a French high-speed service.

clue.text: Leaves goalie sprawling after final's start

start picks the opening letter of final
sprawling suggests the letters are spread out in disorder

explanation.surface: A keeper sprawling as the cup final kicks off.

explanation.definitionFit: The leaves of plants taken collectively; a synonym.

clue.text: Fried food is healthier? That's about right

parts.note: fitter means in better health

clue.text: Destitute family put into street

parts.note: kin are one's family

explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for penniless; a synonym for destitute.

clue.text: Single babes losing heart for stars

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter is removed from the babes word

parts.note: dolls is slang for attractive young women, babes

clue.text: Flash skin of pectorals showing muscles

parts.note: a trice is an instant, as in 'in a flash'

indicators.note: skin of picks the outer letters of the word, as skin is on the outside

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder shows off his chest muscles.

clue.text: Put in military unit, journalist receives medal

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

clue.text: Rise in current is correct

parts.note: a tide is a current of water

clue.text: Programme of actors with bad cast

clue.text: Reportedly hatched offspring

parts.note: brewed means plotted, as in a scheme hatched

explanation.surface: A newly hatched family of chicks, so we hear.

clue.text: Language is blunt, losing head

parts.note: terse means curt or blunt

clue.text: Drinking red I entertained, taking part
